interest: This document illustrates the intense security sensitivity and surveillance surrounding military and naval installations in pre-war Japan, where foreign diplomats and military attachés faced constant scrutiny. It highlights how an everyday occurrence—traveling by train past the naval air station near Kure—could swiftly escalate into formal accusations of espionage and illicit photography, necessitating high-level diplomatic explanations to the Japanese Foreign Office. Additionally, it offers insight into the State Department's cross-referencing and filing system, directing researchers from general cultural/technical classifications to specific personnel or diplomatic incident files.
overview: This file consists of a single list-of-papers docket sheet for decimal file 894.4035 (Social Matters: Fine Arts: Japan: Photography). It catalogues a single entry, despatch No. 2073 from diplomat Erle R. Dickover in Japan, concerning allegations that Lieutenant Ralph A. Ofstie, Assistant American Naval Attaché to Japan, took photographs from a train while passing the naval air station near Kure. The entry notes that a memorandum was submitted to the Japanese Foreign Office explaining that no photographs were taken, and directs researchers to the primary documentation cross-referenced under decimal file 121.5594/76.

subfiles.summary: This docket sheet records entry No. 1 under subject classification 894.4035 (Photography - Japan). It references despatch No. 2073 from Erle R. Dickover dated October 9 concerning accusations that Assistant American Naval Attaché Ralph A. Ofstie took illicit photographs while on a train passing the naval air station near Kure. The entry notes that a copy of a memorandum explaining that no photographs had been taken was submitted to the Japanese Foreign Office, and provides a cross-reference to 121.5594/76.
